name: Kiphendé, 'de taal van de Aphende'
confidence_why: One first-hand description, checked against the source; 4 other works consulted do not discuss stress.
catalog_citation: Stappers, Leo (1953). De toongroepen en hun wijzigingen in de taal van de Aphende. Kongo-Overzee 19(4): 376-379. (open scan:https://archive.org/details/sim_kongo-overzee_1953_19_4)
catalog_locator: p. 376, opening paragraphs; tone-change rules pp. 377-378
catalog_quote: De taal der Apende, het Kiphendé heeft twee grondtonen: een gelijkmatige hoge en lage toon. Het toonsysteem is „syllabisch-stationnair” en behoort tot het etymologisch type. De monosyllabische stammen vallen uiteen in twee toongroepen naargelang op de kern een hoge of lage grondtoon rust. De toongroepen of in feite voorkomende combinaties van grondtonen bij de tweeklankgrepen tellende stammen, zijn vier in getal: IA laag-laag, IB laag-hoog, IIA hoog-laag en IIB hoog-hoog. Het prefix heeft in onbeïnvloede positie een lage toon. De ongewijzigde grondtonen der toongroepen vinden we in de constructie: onderwerp van een werkwoordelijke zin.
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

new_statements.translation: The language of the Apende, Kiphendé, has two basic tones: a level high and a level low tone. The tone system is 'syllabic-stationary' and belongs to the etymological type. Monosyllabic stems fall into two tone groups according to whether a high or a low basic tone rests on the nucleus. The tone groups, i.e. the actually occurring combinations of basic tones in disyllabic stems, are four in number: IA low-low, IB low-high, IIA high-low and IIB high-high. The prefix has a low tone in unaffected position.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Phende is described as a two-tone (H/L) language with lexically fixed stem tone patterns (two for monosyllabic stems, four for disyllabic stems) and grammatically conditioned tone changes; no accessible source says anything about word stress (no statement of stress placement, of penultimate prominence or lengthening, or of the absence of stress).
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not mentioned in any accessible source.
new_statements.exceptions: None regarding stress. For tone, Stappers lists construction-dependent changes (prefix becomes H in isolation and as object; falling tone on prefix of group II; stem H lowered to mid in object position, etc.).
new_statements.domain_note: Tone patterns are given for noun and verb stems at word level, with changes stated for the isolated word, genitive rectum/regens and verb-object constructions; Smalley 1958 p. 68 adds only that tone is phonemically pertinent but unwritten. No citation-form or phrase-level stress information exists in the opened sources.
new_statements.identity_note: Stappers 1953 writes from Kamponde (Kasayi), i.e. presumably the eastern (Kasai) Pende; Smalley 1958 distinguishes Western (west of the Kwilu), Central (Kwilu-Loange) and Eastern (east of the Loange) dialect areas differing in consonant phonology; Niyonkuru 1983 describes the 'dialecte de Bandundu'; Bunduki 1965 the Western Pende of Gungu. All are under phen1239; no separate glottocodes for these dialects were found. Glottolog gives Guthrie L11 (Tervuren K52 per Niyonkuru).

sources.note: Nothing on stress/klemtoon. States Kiphende has two level basic tones (H, L), a 'syllabic-stationary' tone system of the etymological type; monosyllabic stems fall into two tone groups, disyllabic stems into four (LL, LH, HL, HH); noun prefix is L in unaffected position; describes tonal changes in isolation, genitive and object constructions and in verb forms.

sources.citation: Niyonkuru, L. (1983). Note sur l'assibilation en pende. Africana Linguistica 9: 265-269. DOI 10.3406/aflin.1983.922.
sources.note: Nothing on stress or tone; consonant reflexes of Proto-Bantu before *i/*u in the Bandundu dialect. Bibliography (p. 269) notes Gusimana's 1972 dictionary exists in a tone-marked version made at Tervuren by G. Mudiji-Malamba, and cites Niyonkuru 1978 (ULB mémoire).

sources.citation: Gusimana, Barthélemy (1972). Dictionnaire pende-français. Bandundu: CEEBA. Tone-marked version prepared at Tervuren by G. Mudiji-Malamba (per Niyonkuru 1983: 269); CBOLD electronic copy.
sources.note: The CEEBA dictionary introduction (xxiii pp.) is the likeliest place for a note on tone marking, vowel length and accent; the CBOLD copy was downloadable until the site died. Internet Archive copy exists but is could not be reached by automated download.

sources.note: Overview of Bantu tone; cites Phende [L11] as a Kongo-area language with 'tone cases': a /0-H/ stem /-kunzú/ 'basket' has gi-kunzú (default: citation, subject), gí-kunzú (predicative 'it's a basket'), gí-kú'nzú (object of affirmative verb: H spreads to the first stem syllable creating a following downstep); 'Phende in fact makes a five-way distinction in tone patterns on nouns (Hyman 2017b:113)', likely reflecting the *H of the augment and of predicative *ní. Secondary for Phende beyond these examples; nothing on stress.
